---
title: "CSIL History Archive"
subtitle: "A public history of Choice in Supports for Independent Living in British Columbia"
toc: false
---

**Choice in Supports for Independent Living (CSIL)** is a British Columbia home-support program. Eligible people can receive public funding and use it to hire their own workers, instead of receiving care only through an agency.

This site is a public history of how that idea developed. It is written from sources we can cite — newspapers, Hansard, later government reports, training materials, and accounts from people and organizations involved. Today's program web pages describe how CSIL works now. They are not, by themselves, a history of how CSIL was designed, first tried, or later changed.

The history is incomplete on purpose. Pages distinguish what a source documents, what someone later remembered, what we infer, where sources disagree, and what is still an open question. We do not yet know a single start year. Later writers treat **1993 or 1994** as the year CSIL was established. Later official records describe a **1994 pilot** and **province-wide availability in 1995**. A **1995** newspaper still described CSIL as a new pilot program. This site shows that disagreement rather than hiding it.

One useful way to read the chapters — as a possible order of events, **not** a settled history — is:

**care in institutions or through agencies → independent-living experiments led by disabled people → Creekview → the Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM) → funding that followed the person → CSIL designed and piloted → a province-wide program.**

The chapters reconstruct Creekview, ECPM, CSIL's early years, and later changes from public sources. None of them treats Creekview → ECPM → CSIL as a proven official sequence. A short [summary of what the evidence does and does not show](history/index.qmd#state-of-the-evidence) lives on the History page.

This archive is meant for CSIL employers, disability advocates, researchers, journalists, policy staff, and people who took part in that history. It is not a campaign, and it is not a guide to applying for CSIL.

If you can help, the most useful contributions are citations, catalogue records, copies of public documents we are still looking for, and corrections. Please read [About / Contribute](about.qmd#how-to-contribute) and do not send private or health-related records.
